cells.line: so a late guest may enter.

readings.rationale: “may” and “enter” read as an opening, while a guard could still make the permission conditional.

cells.line: so a late guest must enter.

readings.implied_speaker: a host urging a traveler into shelter before a storm
readings.rationale: “guest” suggests a hosting relation; “must” supplies urgency; “enter” points toward shelter only once the storm setting is supplied. Counter-reading: the same host may be coercing someone who prefers to leave.

supplied_speakers: a host urging a traveler into shelter before a storm

cells.line: so a late guest may wait outside.

readings.implied_speaker: the person who brought a chair outside and stayed with the guest in #11607
readings.rationale: “may” leaves waiting optional and “outside” names a place, not whether the guest is alone. This context-dependent speaker comes from the chair poem in #11607, not from the isolated C line. It can be hospitality without admission.

supplied_speakers: the person who brought a chair outside and stayed with the guest in #11607
